thread:
maria.g: heads-up — seeing a weird IO latency staircase on ephemeral NVMe during last batch window in us-west1, started ~03:12 UTC, affects ~8 GPU nodes
jonathan.k: same, noticed queued iops climb then plateau in 1-2min steps
maria.g: quick iostat snapshot (abridged):
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rMB/s   wMB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1          0.50  1200.00   0.00    6.00    5.12    8.45  12.3  0.08 98.7
```
alex: that avgqu-sz ~8 is the red flag. any janitor/scrub overlap?
jess: scrub scheduler kicked a rolling pass at 03:10 (eu->us stagger) but one shard hit us-west around the same time
maria.g: looks like janitor deletes + checkpoint writes from batch reclaim overlapped on a subset of nodes -> write amplification + queue buildup
jonathan.k: mitigation — throttled scrub to 10% on the affected pool, latency dropped back in ~90s
maria.g: applied via feature-flag: scrub.rate=0.1 (rolled to us-west1)
alex: can we also rate-limit reclaim or add a soft backoff when avgqu-sz > 5? otherwise next batch window will re-trigger
maria.g: opened INFRA-2219 to add reclaim backoff and a scheduler headroom check; increased stagger to 30s between janitor shards as immediate change
sre-bot: deploybot: feature-flag scrub.rate=0.1 rolled to us-west1 at 03:20 UTC :white_check_mark:
jonathan.k: proposal for follow-up: alert on avgqu-sz > 6 for 2m, and a 3-tier throttle (10%, 25%, off) based on queue depth
maria.g: agreed. assigning to @alex and @jess to own the headroom check + alerting, will update INFRA-2219. thanks :thumbsup:
